accent2.note: Unchanged by the green rotation - it was already the cool half of the pair, and at 182deg it stays 48deg clear of the accent.

hueRamp.purpose: The entire hued surface system. Twenty-four tab hues and seven project-link hues derive from these eight properties and nothing else; retune here, nowhere else. Chroma is held near --fg-dim's (~0.021 oklch) so hue still identifies a control without leaving the Hazard palette, and lightness does the contrast work. Measured across all 26 hues ON A SCANLINE ROW: text >= 5.7:1, every border >= 3.3:1. The two preset download buttons derive from this block too, at hues 245 and 165.

display.purpose: The `welcome :3` heading only. The one gradient on the page.

headline.purpose: Preset and section titles inside content panels.

title.purpose: Section headings and prominent tab-panel headings.

body.purpose: Long preset explanations, changelog notes, and option copy. Capped at 78ch.

label.purpose: Tab labels, download links, resource names, compact controls.

micro.purpose: Statusline, link info, captions, version metadata, badges, table labels.

shadows.name: flat-reset
shadows.purpose: Applied via a global `*` rule. There is no elevation system; anything added later arrives flat.

shadows.name: favicon-drop
shadows.purpose: The hero pixel favicon, and the only glow on a component. Mirrors the extension's single mascot drop-shadow.

shadows.name: statusline-bloom
shadows.purpose: Phosphor bloom on the statusline, the one text-shadow the flat reset gives back. Part of the CRT overlay.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default color, border, and background hover transitions.

motion.name: tooltip-transition
motion.purpose: The link-info popover on the hero pills.

motion.name: rainbow-shift
motion.purpose: The hero gradient. Frozen under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: flicker
motion.purpose: CRT overlay. Dips to 92% opacity for one frame every four seconds. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

palette.basis: Hazard Console (SillyBunny-Terminal-UI style.css:303), hue family rotated to 140deg.
palette.method: Every token keeps the original's lightness and chroma; only the hue moved. That is why all 26 tab hues, every border and every text pair still clear contrast after the recolour without a single other edit. Recolour again the same way: rotate the hue, leave L and C alone.

components.name: Statusline
components.description: Sticky one-line bar carrying the counts that actually change. Counts are recomputed from the DOM on load so they cannot drift.
components.css: .ds-statusline { position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 50; width: 100%; padding: 6px 10px; background: #232c22; border-block-end: 1px solid #5f8f55; color: #94a491; font: 600 0.76rem/1.2 ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; letter-spacing: 0.01em; text-align: center; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-statusline::before { content: "purachina's stuff | "; }

components.name: Project Link
components.description: Top-level project link. Keeps a hue from the ramp for identity; Ko-fi is the exception and takes console green outright.
components.html: SynapselocalStorage AI assistant frontend
components.css: .ds-project-link { --pill-hue: 245; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 36px; padding: 0.32rem 0.95rem; text-decoration: none; letter-spacing: 0.01em; color: oklch(0.72 0.038 var(--pill-hue)); border: 1px solid oklch(0.50 0.038 var(--pill-hue)); background: oklch(0.25 0.016 var(--pill-hue)); font: 400 0.83rem/1.4 ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace; transition: color 0.25s, border-color 0.25s, background 0.25s; } .ds-project-link:hover { color: oklch(0.89 0.045 var(--pill-hue)); border-color: oklch(0.66 0.055 var(--pill-hue)); background: oklch(0.30 0.024 var(--pill-hue)); } .ds-link-info { color: oklch(0.62 0.026 var(--pill-hue)); font-size: 0.68rem; }

components.name: Tab Label
components.description: Radio-label tab used for preset sections, platform switching, and sub-tabs. Selected state inverts rather than glowing.
components.css: .ds-tab { --pill-hue: 145; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 44px; padding: 0.4rem 1.3rem; cursor: pointer; user-select: none; white-space: nowrap; color: oklch(0.72 0.028 var(--pill-hue)); border: 1px solid oklch(0.58 0.028 var(--pill-hue)); background: oklch(0.24 0.012 var(--pill-hue)); font: 400 0.8rem/1.4 ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace; transition: color 0.25s, border-color 0.25s, background 0.25s; } .ds-tab:hover { color: oklch(0.90 0.036 var(--pill-hue)); border-color: oklch(0.62 0.048 var(--pill-hue)); background: oklch(0.29 0.020 var(--pill-hue)); } .ds-tab-active { color: #141a13; font-weight: 700; border-color: oklch(0.74 0.055 var(--pill-hue)); background: oklch(0.74 0.055 var(--pill-hue)); }

components.name: Download Button
components.description: Secondary downloads are bracketed. The two current preset downloads take the terminal primary idiom and each wears its platform, using the same desaturated fill the switcher uses when that platform is selected. Brackets or an icon, never both.
components.html: Regex SetDownload 15.1 (SillyTavern)Download 15.1 (SillyBunny)
components.css: .ds-download { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 44px; padding: 0.5rem 1.4rem; text-decoration: none; color: #dee8dc; border: 1px solid #5f8f55; background: #232c22; font: 400 0.8rem/1.4 ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace; transition: color 0.25s, border-color 0.25s, background 0.25s; } .ds-download::before { content: '[\00a0' / ''; color: #94a491; } .ds-download::after { content: '\00a0]' / ''; color: #94a491; } .ds-download:hover { color: #a0e570; border-color: #a0e570; background: #141a13; } .ds-download-primary { --pill-hue: 245; padding: 0.6rem 1.6rem; font-weight: 700; color: #141a13; border-color: oklch(0.74 0.055 var(--pill-hue)); background: oklch(0.74 0.055 var(--pill-hue)); } .ds-download-primary.ds-sb { --pill-hue: 165; } .ds-download-primary::before, .ds-download-primary::after { content: none; } .ds-download-primary:hover { color: oklch(0.74 0.055 var(--pill-hue)); border-color: oklch(0.74 0.055 var(--pill-hue)); background: #141a13; }

components.name: Resource Card
components.description: Flat bordered panel for extensions, themes, options, and cards. Hover moves the border to console green; there is no glow. The teal sigil marks a named thing.

components.name: CRT Overlay
components.description: Fixed over the viewport above everything including the lightbox, with pointer-events: none so it never intercepts a click. Deliberately faint - turning it up is how a terminal skin becomes a costume.
components.css: body::after { content: ''; position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 400; pointer-events: none; background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, rgba(2, 4, 3, 0.08) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px); animation: flicker 4s infinite; } @keyframes flicker { 0%, 97%, 100% { opacity: 1; } 98% { opacity: 0.92; } } .statusline { text-shadow: 0 0 2px var(--glow); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { body::after { animation: none; } } @media (forced-colors: active), (prefers-contrast: more) { body::after { display: none; } }

narrative.overview: The root site is a personal bench of useful things: presets, tools, cards, themes, screenshots, and blunt notes laid out for people who already know why they came here. The bench now sits in a terminal: the Hazard Console palette from SillyBunny-Terminal-UI rotated green, wearing that extension's chrome - monospace throughout, no corner radius, no shadows, 1px moss hairlines, and `>` sigils that mark where a thing begins. Terminal conventions are here to clarify state, not to decorate. The design rejects corporate SaaS polish, generic AI landing-page aesthetics, oversized marketing hero sections, vague value-prop copy, and anything that makes the site feel like a startup pitch.
keyCharacteristics: A statusline pinned at the top carrying the counts that actually change.
A compact centered landing stack that quickly gives way to functional tabs and downloads.
Monospace-only typography with weight, not colour, doing the hierarchy.
Flat bordered controls throughout. Selection inverts rather than glowing.
Olive surfaces with hazard-yellow accents and desaturated per-project hues, all at one chroma.
A CRT scanline over the whole page - 1px every 3px at 8%, flickering once every four seconds.

rules.name: The Useful Color Rule
rules.body: Colored accents identify a project, platform, or state. Do not add decorative accent colors to ordinary information blocks.

rules.name: The One Chroma Rule
rules.body: New hued surfaces derive from the ramp. A colour at higher chroma than --fg-dim reads as a foreign object unless it is genuinely content - a theme swatch, a game crest, a card thumbnail.

rules.name: The Rainbow Exception Rule
rules.body: The animated rainbow heading is the one gradient on the page, and the one loud flourish. Do not repeat gradient text or gradient fills anywhere else.

rules.name: The Green Means Act Rule
rules.body: Console green marks the thing to do or the thing in focus. Teal marks the thing with a name. Neither is decoration.

rules.name: The Rotation Rule
rules.body: The palette is Hazard Console with one number changed - the hue. Recolour by rotating the hue family and leaving every lightness and chroma alone; that is what carried all 26 tab hues through the green move with no other edit.

rules.name: The Compact Hub Rule
rules.body: Do not introduce oversized marketing typography beyond the existing hero. Most new content belongs at title, body, label, or micro scale.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Monospace is the whole voice. There is no second family and no reason for one - code snippets are already in the same face as everything around them.

rules.name: The 78ch Rule
rules.body: Monospace runs unreadable past about eighty characters. Prose blocks cap at 78ch, the same figure the extension uses.

rules.name: No Uppercasing
rules.body: text-transform appears nowhere. Uppercase labels were a Figtree-era device and are gone.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: No radius, no shadow, no blur, no gradient. If a new component needs to stand out, give it a border, a surface step, or inversion. The favicon drop-shadow, the rainbow hero and the CRT overlay are screen furniture, not components; a new one is not a licence for a fourth.

rules.name: The Outline Rule
rules.body: Focus is drawn with outline, never box-shadow, so it survives the flat reset. 2px solid var(--accent) at 2px offset, everywhere. Keyboard focus must stay at least as visible as hover.

rules.name: The Border Strength Rule
rules.body: Component outlines take --border at full strength; only separators inside an already-bounded box drop to --hairline. Nothing weaker clears 3:1 on both surfaces.

rules.name: The Scanline Rule
rules.body: Measure contrast on a scanline row, not on the flat surface. The overlay darkens text and background together and costs roughly half a point of ratio - enough that --fg-dim and --border both had to be lifted a step when it went in.

dos: Do lead with presets, downloads, changelogs, project links, screenshots, and cards before adding new personality flourishes.
Do keep the blunt, personal, tinkerer-made voice in visible copy, especially version notes and resource descriptions.
Do make current versions, previous versions, changelog entries, and platform differences obvious.
Do use the existing flat-panel, label, table, gallery, and lightbox vocabulary before inventing a new component shape.
Do derive any new hued surface from the ramp rather than picking a colour by eye.
Do preserve readable contrast, responsive wrapping, keyboard access, visible focus states, meaningful image alt text, and reduced-motion-friendly behavior.
Do let tools like Synapse keep their own product-specific context and denser app patterns. Synapse is not part of this system.
donts: Don't make the root hub feel like corporate SaaS polish.
Don't use generic AI landing-page aesthetics, oversized marketing hero sections, vague value-prop copy, or sterile template grids.
Don't make the page feel like a startup pitch.
Don't overdecorate the root hub until presets, programs, and downloads become harder to find.
Don't reintroduce radius, shadow, blur, or gradient. The rainbow hero and the CRT overlay are the whole allowance.

Don't add terminal decoration for its own sake - no ASCII art, no box-drawing frames, no CRT scanline. The extension ships its scanline off by default and names decorative CRT clutter an anti-reference.
Don't turn every repeated item into a same-sized icon card grid.
Don't restyle anything inside a prompting-lab transcript body. The <font color> dialogue and inline-styled tracker blocks are captured model output - they are the sample.
